blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.
blocks.zh: 在大型语言模型(LLM)代理生成出一件文物后,用户经常会为它发送编辑请求. 本文研究了LLM在发出这些请求之前是否能够预见到这些请求. 这种预期在实践中是有用的,因为它减少了用户审查和反馈的努力。 我们正式确定这项任务为编辑建议并构建EditRec Bench,这是从WildChat-4.8M中的现实世界对话日志来评价LLMs在这项任务上的表现的基准. 通过基准和失败分析,我们查明了一个实际挑战,即一些案例在现实环境中本来就难以预测。 为了解决这一问题,我们采用了基于决策模型的标注法,在向用户提出预测之前,过滤出预测不大可能正确的情况。 我们训练有素的模型超越了现有的决策模型,并在显示的建议中将通过"5"提升到12-25分的比分. 我们的代码可在https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-advision上查到。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Creating artifacts such as code and documents with a large language model (LLM)-based chat assistant often involves an iterative process: users review the assistant’s output, request changes, and repeat until the artifact meets their expectations.
In this process, the assistant typically waits for users to send an edit request, but what if it could anticipate that request before they send it?
With several likely edit requests shown as clickable suggestions in the chat interface, users could send their intended request with a single click, reducing review and feedback effort.
blocks.zh:
创建诸如有大型语言模型(LLM)的聊天助手的代码和文档等文物往往涉及一个迭接过程:用户审查助理的输出,请求更改,并重复到文物达到预期为止.
在这个过程中,助手一般会等用户发送编辑请求,但如果在他们发送之前可以预见到该请求呢?
在聊天界面中显示一些可能作为可点击建议进行编辑的请求,用户可以一次点击发送其预期请求,减少审查和反馈努力.

blocks.en:
Prior work has studied user utterance prediction in the broader context of human–LLM conversations. Naous et al. (2026) have proposed an LLM reproducing user turns to support realistic user simulation,
while other studies have explored predicting next user prompts from conversational context Goren et al. (2025) ; Chen et al. (2026) ; Kim et al. (2026) .
In production, Codex and Claude Code have introduced features that suggest users’ next prompts OpenAI (2026b) ; Anthropic (2025) .
blocks.zh:
以前的工作研究了在更广泛的人类-LLM对话背景下的用户言论预测。 Naous等人(2026年)提议使用LLM复制用户转折,以支持现实的用户模拟,
其他研究也探索了从对话背景Goren等人(2025年);Chen等人(2026年);Kim等人(2026年)预测下一个用户提示。
在制作中,Codex和Claude Code引入了提示用户下个提示OpenAI(2026b;Anthropic (2025))的功能.

blocks.en:
In contrast to these general prompt predictions, this paper focuses on predicting edit requests, which is practically useful in conversational artifact generation.
We formalize this prediction task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating whether an LLM can predict users’ actual edit requests from the preceding context. The data is sampled from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M Zhao et al. (2024) .
We also propose a new evaluation criterion specifically designed for edit requests that compares the edit locations and content of predicted and actual edit requests.
We evaluate eight LLMs (gpt-oss-20b/120b, Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, Llama 3.1, gpt-6-luna, etc.) on the benchmark, using Claude Haiku 5.5 for LLM-as-a-Judge.
The results show that the models follow a similar ranking to that observed on other benchmarks, with pass@5 ranging from 10% to 47%.
blocks.zh:
与这些一般的即时预测相反,本文侧重于预测编辑请求,这在对话出产文物时实际上有用.
我们正式确定这项预测任务, 作为编辑建议和构建 EditRec Bench , 这是评估 LLM 是否能够从上下文预测用户实际编辑请求的基准 。 数据取自WildChat-4.8M中真实世界的对话记录 赵等 (2024).
我们还提出了专门为编辑请求而设计的新的评价标准,该标准比较了预测和实际编辑请求的编辑地点和内容。
我们利用Claude Haiku 5.5的LLM-as-a-Judge,对8个LLM(gpt-oss-20b/120b、Quen3.5-9B、Gemma 4 12B、Llama 3.1、gpt-6-luna等)进行基准评价。
结果显示,这些模型的排名与其他基准的排名相似,通过率从10%到47%不等。

blocks.en:
Furthermore, our failure analysis reveals that some real-world edit requests are inherently difficult to anticipate from context alone.
This indicates that simply offering suggestions every time may be counterproductive, as frequent incorrect suggestions could degrade the user experience in practice.
We therefore introduce decision model-based gating to skip suggestions for such difficult samples, thereby improving pass@5 of the shown suggestions.
Specifically, we fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B as a decision model using the training split. Our gating model outperforms other statistical methods and decision models, and improves pass@5 on shown suggestions by 12–25 points at the threshold showing 20% of dev samples.
blocks.zh:
此外,我们的失败分析显示,一些现实世界的编辑请求本身就难以从上下文中预测。
这表明,只要每次都提出建议可能适得其反,因为频繁的错误建议可能会降低用户的实际经验。
因此,我们采用基于决定模式的标点法,以跳过关于这些困难样本的建议,从而改进所示建议的通过@5。
具体地说,我们用训练分开来微调了Quen3.5-4B作为决定模式. 我们的标注模型比其他统计方法和决策模型要好, 并且改进了在显示20%的脱氧核糖核酸样本的阈值上,

blocks.en: In summary, our contributions are threefold: • We propose a new benchmark for evaluating the ability of LLMs to anticipate edit requests from users in real-world datasets (§ 2 ). • We evaluate eight LLMs on the benchmark and validate the task feasibility. We also find that some real-world edit requests are inherently difficult to anticipate from context alone (§ 3 ). • We propose decision model-based gating to skip suggestions for inherently difficult samples, thereby improving pass@5 of the shown suggestions (§ 4 ).

blocks.en: 2.2 Data curation
blocks.zh: 2.2 国家 数据解析

blocks.en:
We curate data samples from WildChat-4.8M Zhao et al. (2024) , which includes real-world conversation logs between ChatGPT models and users collected between April 2023 and July 2025.
The curation pipeline consists of multiple stages: rule-based pre-screening, LLM-based sample extraction, sample refinement, and data split. In the following, we describe the overview of each stage.
blocks.zh:
我们整理来自WildChat-4.8M的数据样本 Zhao等 (2024),包括ChatGPT模型与2023年4月至2025年7月收集的用户之间的真实世界对话日志.
校正管由多个阶段组成:基于规则的预筛选,基于LLM的取样,取样精炼,数据分解. 下面我们介绍每个阶段的概况。

blocks.en:
We apply rule-based pre-screening to retain only samples that are mostly in English, contain no toxic or redacted content, and include a user turn following an assistant turn.
We also exclude users whose traffic suggests automated activity or account sharing.
To prevent highly active users from dominating the dataset, we retain at most three conversations per user.
After pre-screening, 97,965 conversations remain.
blocks.zh:
我们采用基于规则的预筛选,只保留大部分为英文的样本,不含有毒或被修改的内容,并包括一个助手转接后的用户转接.
我们还排除其流量建议自动活动或账户共享的用户。
为了防止高度活跃的用户主导数据集,我们每个用户最多保留了三次对话.
经过预先筛选后,97,965个对话仍然存在.

blocks.en:
For each conversation, an LLM (gpt-oss-120b in this paper) reads the whole conversation, lists every edit request, and takes the last one as the edit request e e of a sample.
The turns before it form the preceding context c c , and the turns after it are discarded.
To help the LLM identify e e , we prompt it to extract e e along with the artifacts appearing immediately before and after e e .
We repeat this process three times and retain only samples ( c , e ) (c,e) for which all three runs identify the same e e .
This yields 18,992 samples.
blocks.zh:
对于每次对话,一个LLM(本文中的gpt-oss-120b)会读取整个对话,列出每一个编辑请求,并将最后一个作为样本的编辑请求e.
其前转向形成前上下文cc,后转向被丢弃.
为了帮助LLM识别e e,我们促使它提取e 以及e 前后出现的文物.
我们重复三次这一过程,只保留样本(c,e)(c,e),所有三个运行都标明相同的e。
这个样本的产量为18,992个。

blocks.en:
We further filter out samples ( c , e ) (c,e) if either of the artifacts extracted from immediately before and after e e is empty, the two artifacts are identical, either artifact differs by more than 10% from its corresponding assistant response, or the artifact preceding e e contains fewer than 300 characters.
With assistance from Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, we also manually remove any ethically problematic and ambiguous samples remaining after the preceding processes.
Finally, we draw one sample per user at random, which yields 12,298 samples.
See Appendix E for data validation.

在Claude Fable 5.1和Opus 5.5的协助下,我们还手动移除了上述过程之后在道德上有问题和含糊不清的样本。
最后,我们随机抽取每个用户一个样本,得出12,298个样本。

We then define the requirements for each finalized sample using an LLM (Claude Haiku 5.5 in this paper).
For the edit request e e of each sample, the LLM first generates a set of requirements. It then evaluates whether e ^ \hat{e} , a paraphrase of e e , satisfies these requirements.
Since e ^ \hat{e} is essentially the same request as e e , it is expected to satisfy them. If the requirements are satisfied, we finalize the set.
Otherwise, the LLM keeps revising and evaluating it until the requirements are satisfied or a total of three iterations is reached. If the requirements remain unsatisfied after the third iteration, we adopt the final set.
blocks.zh:
然后,我们用一个LLM(本文中的Claude Haiku 5.5)来确定每个最后样本的要求。
对于每个样本的编辑请求e,LLM首先生成一组要求. 然后,它评估e的一说e是否满足了这些要求。
由于e ^\ hat{e} 基本上与e e 相同,因此可望满足它们。 如果满足了要求,我们最终确定这套程序。
否则,LLM会不断修订和评价它,直到满足要求或总共达到三次重复. 如果第三次复会后各项要求仍未得到满足,我们就采用最后一套。

blocks.en: 3 Benchmark Evaluation
blocks.zh: 3 基准评价

blocks.en: In this section, we describe evaluation settings on the benchmark, show the results, and discuss real-world challenges through failure analysis.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们介绍基准上的评价设置,显示结果,并通过失败分析讨论现实世界的挑战。

blocks.en: 3.1 Settings
blocks.zh: 3.1 设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate eight LLMs:
Llama 3.1 8B Grattafiori et al. (2024) ,
UserLM-8b Naous et al. (2026) ,
Qwen3.5-9B Qwen Team (2026) ,
Gemma 4 12B Gemma Team et al. (2026) ,
gpt-oss-20b/120b OpenAI et al. (2025) ,
gpt-6-luna OpenAI (2026c) ,
gpt-6.1-sol OpenAI (2026d) .
We enable reasoning and set the effort to medium for supported models.
For all other parameters, we use the recommended settings.
Each open model is served with vLLM Kwon et al. (2023) on one or two RTX A6000 GPUs (48GB).
In addition to LLMs, we also evaluate two rule-based baselines: Shuffled returns the five predictions that gpt-oss-120b made for another, randomly assigned sample, which gives the chance level of matching; Stock requests returns the same five generic or popular edit requests for every sample.
See Appendix B for details of models and parameters.

blocks.en:
We use Claude Haiku 5.5 Anthropic (2026) with medium reasoning effort as an LLM judge.
Given the preceding context, the actual edit request, and k k predicted edit requests, the judge evaluates whether any of the predictions are essentially equivalent to the actual request based on the annotated requirements.
Extra details in a predicted edit request are allowed as long as they do not conflict with the actual request.
We repeat this evaluation three times and set max i ≤ k ⁡ match ⁡ ( e i ′ , e ) = 1 \max_{i\leq k}\mathrm{match}(e^{\prime}_{i},e)=1 in Eq. ( 2 ) if at least two votes are positive. As a result, 98.8% of individual votes agree with the majority decision, and all three votes agree on 96.3% of samples, indicating high consistency of the LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations.
See Appendix F for the validation of LLM-as-a-Judge.

To address the problem, we introduce decision model-based gating.
After LLM predictors predict K K edit requests, it evaluates whether they include the actual edit request to decide whether to show them. They are shown to the user only if they pass the gate.
This enables selective suggestions, increasing the likelihood of a match when they are shown.
In the following, we model the gating mechanism and describe how to train a decision model for it.

为了解决这一问题,我们采用了基于决策模式的地标法。

这样可以有选择地提出建议,增加显示建议时匹配的可能性。
在下文中,我们模拟了取景机制,并描述了如何为此培训一个决策模式。

blocks.en: We implement the gating model using a decision model TypeSafe (2026) ; OpenAI (2026a) , which enables cost-efficient classification.

A decision model takes natural-language instructions and outputs a probability between 0 and 1 for each option specified in the output schema.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduced a benchmark for evaluating LLMs’ ability to predict users’ next edit requests. Benchmarking and failure analysis revealed that some requests are inherently difficult to predict, motivating decision model-based gating to selectively show suggestions. Our trained gating model improved pass@5 among shown suggestions over baselines.
We believe this paper contributes from both a research perspective, by revealing LLMs’ ability on the new task, and a practical perspective, by proposing a deployment strategy for edit recommendation in chat systems.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们提出了评价LLMs预测用户下次编辑请求能力的基准. 基准和失败分析显示,有些请求本来就难以预测,促使基于决策模式的标注有选择地显示建议。 我们训练有素的钓鱼模式改进了通过量,
我们认为本文既从研究角度,揭示LLMs在新任务方面的能力,又从实际角度,提出在聊天系统中编辑建议的部署战略。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our gating model requires both the preceding context and the predicted edit requests, so it cannot avoid the LLM predictor’s inference cost even when suggestions are not shown to the user. As shown in Appendix H , the preceding context alone provides insufficient information for reliable gating, highlighting the importance of the predicted edit requests.
Nevertheless, we consider that these costs are modest: with gpt-6-luna as the predictor, one list of five predicted edit requests costs about USD 0.0006 and takes a median of 4.0 s, and the gating model adds only 0.43 s on a single GPU.
blocks.zh:
我们的取笑模型既需要前一种上下文,也需要预测的编辑请求,因此即使没有向用户显示建议,它也无法避免LLM预测器的推论成本. 如附录H所显示的,仅上下文就不足以提供可靠的定位信息,突出了预测编辑请求的重要性.
然而,我们认为这些成本是微小的:以gpt-6-luna为预测器,列出一份5个预测编辑请求,费用约为0.06美元并取中位数为4.0秒,而标注模型在一个GPU上只增加0.43秒.

blocks.en: We do not conduct a user study to quantify how the fraction of samples shown and pass@5 affect user experience. Instead, we evaluate our method using objective metrics, including pass@ k k and the fraction of samples shown. These results demonstrate its effectiveness under our offline evaluation but do not establish its impact on user experience.
blocks.zh: 我们不进行用户研究,以量化显示和通过样本的分数@5如何影响用户经验。 相反,我们使用客观的衡量标准来评估我们的方法,包括通过@kk和所显示的样本的分量。 这些结果表明,根据我们的离线评价,这一结果很有效,但对用户经验没有影响。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
EditRecBench is built from WildChat-4.8M, which is released under the ODC-BY license and de-identified by its authors.
We use the data in accordance with its ODC-BY license, cite its source, and refer to the original conversations by their hashes so that the dataset’s removal requests also apply to our samples.
In addition to the dataset’s filter, we apply our own additional filters using LLM checks, keyword lists, and scans for credentials and personal secrets, manually reviewing all scan matches. This removes any sample with ethically problematic content.
When in doubt, we removed the sample.
In terms of the risks of the task itself, this study only asks LLMs to predict filtered edit requests for artifacts, so we do not expect the prediction task itself to cause direct harm.
blocks.zh:
EditRec Bench由WildChat-4.8M所建,根据ODC-BY许可证发行并被其作者去识别.
我们根据ODC-BY许可使用数据, 引用其来源,
除了数据集的过滤器之外,我们使用我们自己的额外过滤器,使用LLM检查,关键词列表,以及扫描证书和个人秘密,手动审查所有扫描匹配. 这样可以删除任何带有道德问题内容的样本.
当怀疑的时候,我们移除了样本。
在任务本身的风险方面,本研究只要求LLMs预测被过滤的对文物的编辑请求,因此我们并不期望预测任务本身会造成直接伤害.

blocks.en: Appendix A Related Work
blocks.zh: 附录A 相关工作

blocks.en:
Predicting user utterances supports efficient interaction with conversational systems. ChaI-TeA Goren et al. (2025) studies message autocompletion from conversation history and a typed prefix. OnePred Chen et al. (2026) predicts subsequent queries through recursive intent memory, while UserLM Naous et al. (2026) learns to reproduce user turns for realistic simulation.
PromptHelper Kim et al. (2026) recommends diverse follow-up prompts to support exploration during writing.
On the other hand, our work focuses on edit-request prediction, enabling a concrete evaluation criterion based on where and how users request changes. EditRecBench also includes requests introducing previously unstated information, whereas OnePred’s benchmark selects queries whose intent and key information can be inferred from the preceding context.
In addition to evaluating prediction capabilities, we identify challenges in deploying edit recommendation in chat systems and propose decision model-based gating for selective recommendation.
blocks.zh:
预测用户的语音支持与对话系统的有效互动。 ChAI-TeA Goren等 (2025)从对话历史中研究消息自动补全以及一个打入的前缀. 一张纸 Chen等 (2026)通过递归意图内存预测后续的查询,而UserLM Naous等 (2026)学习再现用户转折进行现实模拟.
提示帮助器 Kim等人(2026年)建议采用多种后续提示,支持写作期间的探索.
另一方面,我们的工作侧重于编辑-请求预测,从而能够根据用户要求改变的地点和方式制定具体的评价标准。 EditRec Bench 还包括介绍以前未说明的信息的请求,而 OnePred 的基准选择了可从前一种上下文推断出意图和关键信息的查询。
除了评价预测能力外,我们还发现在聊天系统中部署编辑建议方面存在的挑战,并提议以决策模型为依据进行选择性建议。

blocks.en:
Artifact revision has been studied across various domains.
IteraTeR ( Du et al., 2022 ) models iterative text
revisions across domains and edit intentions, while CoEdIT ( Raheja et al., 2023 ) edits text according to natural-language
instructions.
For long, structured documents, LEDGER ( Wang et al., 2026 ) uses dependency-aware graph retrieval to select relevant context and
preserve consistency during editing.
In software engineering, SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) evaluates repository-level code changes for resolving real-world issues.
For conversationally generated artifacts, Kikuta (2026) studies the ability of LLMs to propagate revisions to dependent
elements of artifacts.
These studies address how to revise artifacts and maintain their
quality or consistency.
Our work addresses the complementary question of which revision the
user will request next.

blocks.en:
Selective prediction improves reliability by withholding likely errors. Kamath et al. (2020) train a calibrator for selective question answering, while Smart Reply Kannan et al. (2016) uses a triggering model to identify emails likely to receive replies.
We apply selective prediction to edit recommendation by learning whether predicted edit requests will cover the user’s next edit request.

我们运用选择性的预测来编辑推荐,方法是了解预测的编辑请求是否会覆盖用户的下个编辑请求.

blocks.en: Appendix B Details of Models and Parameters
blocks.zh: 附录B 模型和参数的细节

blocks.en:
Table 4 lists the predictors and their recommended settings.
Every predictor receives the same prompts (Appendix I ) and returns five predicted edit requests in a JSON object. An output that does not parse or validate is retried up to three times with the error fed back, and a sample still without a valid output counts as no match.
The maximum output length is set to 30,000 tokens.
blocks.zh:
表4列出了预测器及其建议设置。
每个预测器都收到相同的提示(Appendix I),并返回JSON对象中的5个预测编辑请求. 不解析或验证的输出会被重试最多三次,并反馈出错误,没有有效输出的样本会算作不匹配.
最大输出长度被设定为3万个令牌.

blocks.en:
In terms of UserLM-8b, we apply a different approach to predict edit requests because it simulates the user’s next turn rather than following a task prompt.
We give it the conversation with the intent “You are a user who wants the assistant to revise its last response.” as the system message and draw five samples of the next user turn as its five predicted edit requests.
blocks.zh:
在UserLM-8b方面,我们采用不同的方法来预测编辑请求,因为它模拟了用户的下个回合而不是遵循任务提示.
我们给它对话的用意是“你是一个用户,希望助理修改其最后的回复。” 作为系统信息,并绘制下个用户转弯的五个样本,作为其五个预测的编辑请求。

blocks.en: Table 4: Recommended settings of the LLM predictors.
blocks.zh: 表4:推荐的LLM预测器设置.

blocks.en: We use Claude Haiku 5.5 with medium effort for defining the requirements and LLM-as-a-Judge.
blocks.zh: 我们使用克洛德·海库·5.5,并作出中等努力,确定要求和LLM-as-a-Judge。

blocks.en: Table 5: The five stock requests of each baseline, in the order they are given to the judge. The popular requests are in the order of the greedy choice.
blocks.zh: 表5:每个基线的5个库存申请,按给法官的顺序排列。 通俗相求以贪取相取为序.

blocks.en:
Table 5 shows the generic and popular stock requests.
The generic requests are five hand-written requests of common kinds.
For the popular requests, we embed the requirement changes of the training samples with bge-base-en-v1.5, cluster them with k k -means ( k = 40 k=40 ), let Claude Haiku 5.5 write one generic edit request per cluster, and choose five of these 40 and the five generic requests greedily by their judged matches on 400 training samples.

表5列出通用和受欢迎的库存申请。
一般请求是5个普通类型的手写请求。
对于受欢迎的请求,我们用bge-base-en-v1.5将培训样本的要求变化嵌入其中,用k-means(k = 40 k=40 = 40)将其组合在一起,让克洛德·海库·5.5每组写出一个通用编辑请求,并根据他们判断的400个培训样本的匹配情况,任意选择这40个样本中的5个和5个通用请求.

blocks.en:
For the gating baselines, d3-mini and pplx-decider-flash-v1.2 are used without fine-tuning through their own inference code, and the OpenAI Decisions API with gpt-6-luna. All three receive the same JSON state and questions as our gating model.
The logistic regression ( L 2 L_{2} regularization, C = 0.3 C=0.3 ) uses TF-IDF features from the last user turn (unigrams and bigrams), the artifact (unigrams), and the five predicted edit requests (unigrams and bigrams).
TF-IDF vectorization uses sublinear term frequency, includes only terms that appear in at least three training samples, and limits each vocabulary to 50,000 terms. Additional features include one-hot encodings of the predictor and artifact type, as well as the logarithms of the number of turns, the artifact size, and the length of the last user turn.

对于取景基线,d3-mini和pplx-decider-flash-v1.2在使用时没有通过自己的推论代码进行微调,OpenAI决定API则使用gpt-6-luna. 所有三个都得到同样的JSON状态和问题 作为我们的取景模式。

blocks.en: Appendix C Details of Data Curation
blocks.zh: 附录C 数据校正细节

blocks.en: In this section, we describe the detailed settings of each curation stage.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们描述每个曲艺阶段的详细设置.

blocks.en:
We use the conversation-level fields provided in WildChat-4.8M to filter samples. The language field indicates the most common language detected across the turns in a conversation, and we keep only samples with language = English . The toxic field is a boolean indicating whether a conversation contains toxic content, and we keep only samples with toxic = false . The redacted field is a boolean indicating whether a conversation contains any turns in which personal information or secrets, such as API keys, have been detected and redacted. We keep only samples with redacted = false .
We also keep only conversations that contain at least one user turn that directly follows an assistant turn, which is a candidate for an edit request e e in the next stage.
To avoid automated traffic and shared accounts, we identify a user by the pair of the hashed_ip field and the user agent in the header field. We then exclude every conversation of a user who meets any of the following conditions: i) four or more users share the same IP address; ii) the IP address has more than 300 conversations; iii) the user has more than six conversations per active day (above the 99th percentile of users); iv) the user’s conversations are in three or more languages; v) the user has more than 200 conversations in total; or vi) one of the user’s conversations has exactly the same content as another conversation in WildChat-4.8M (e.g., templated or repeated inputs). From each remaining user, we keep three conversations at random.
blocks.zh:
我们利用WildChat-4.8M中提供的谈话级别字段过滤样本. 语言字段表示在对话中检测到的跨转弯的最常见语言,我们只保留有语言=英语的样本. 毒场是一个布尔,表明谈话是否含有有毒内容,我们只保留有毒性=虚假的样品。 被编辑的字段是一个布尔字段,表示对话是否包含任何已经检测并编辑过个人信息或秘密,如API密钥的转弯. 我们只保存有被校正为虚假的样本。
我们还只保留包含至少一个直接跟随助手转弯的用户转弯的对话,这是下一个阶段编辑请求e的候选人.
为了避免自动流量和共享账户,我们用hashed_ip字段的对子和头段的用户代理来识别一个用户. 然后,我们排除满足以下任何条件的用户的每一次对话: (一)4个以上用户共用同一个IP地址; (二)IP地址有300多个对话; (三)用户每活一天有6个以上的对话(超过99%的用户); (四)用户的对话有3个或更多语言; (五)用户共有200多个对话; (六)用户的其中1个对话的内容与WildChat-4.8M的另一个对话完全相同(如模板化或重复输入). 每一个剩下的用户,我们都会随机进行三个对话.

blocks.en:
Table 6 shows the comparison between LLM’s labels and one human annotator’s labels for the 150 samples.
Of the 100 samples accepted by the LLM, 93 are labeled clear by the human annotator (i.e., 93% precision).
Of the other seven, five are borderline and two are unrelated.
Agreement between the LLM and the human annotator over all 150 samples is moderate Landis and Koch (1977) : 77% for clear vs. not clear (Cohen’s κ \kappa = .41).
The disagreement comes mostly from samples the LLM rejects as borderline but the human annotator finds clear (28 of 49), which reflects our data curation design: it trades recall for precision, so that the samples it keeps are valid edit requests.
These results confirm that our pipeline successfully curates valid edit requests.

blocks.en: Appendix H Gating without Predicted Requests
blocks.zh: 附录H 无预想请求的约会

blocks.en:
Our gating model takes both the preceding context and the predicted edit requests as input, but could gating be performed using only the preceding context? If so, it could skip LLM predictor inference and reduce inference costs.
To test whether such a gate is feasible, we train the decision model under the same setting as in § 5.1 , but exclude the predicted edit requests from its input.
We compare it with existing decision models given the same context-only input and with our gating model given both the context and the predicted edit requests.
blocks.zh:
我们的取笑模式既以前文为上下文,又以预测的编辑请求作为输入,但只使用前文为上下文就可以取笑吗? 如果是这样,它可以跳过LLM预测推论并降低推论成本.
为了检验这种闸门是否可行,我们在与第5.1节相同的环境下对决策模式进行培训,但将预测的编辑请求排除在其输入之外。
我们以相同的上下文输入与现有的决定模型进行比较,并以上下文和预测的编辑请求与我们的定位模型进行比较。

blocks.en:
Tables 9 and 10 show the results.
Without the predicted edit requests, the existing decision models are at chance level, and even the fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B reaches average AUROCs of only .579 and .567, approximately .11 below the same model with the predicted edit requests.
This indicates that the preceding context alone carries little information on whether the predictions will match.
Therefore, the predicted edit requests are necessary for the gating models.
blocks.zh:
表9和表10显示了结果。
如果没有预测的编辑请求,现有的决定模型就处于偶然水平,即使是微调的Quen3.5-4B也只达到平均AUROCs为579和567,与预测的编辑请求相比,大约低于同模型的11.
这表明,仅上述情况本身,对预测是否相符的信息就很少。
因此,预测的编辑请求对于地标模型是必要的.

blocks.en: ⬇ You annotate real conversations between users and AI assistants for a benchmark . The benchmark asks a model to predict , right after the assistant has given an output , how the user will ask for that output to be changed . Your labels decide which user turns become test cases . A wrong case is worse than a missed one , so keep only clear cases . A user turn is a revision request when it asks the assistant to change the output in the assistant turn right before it , so that the reply is a changed version of that same output : corrected , shortened or lengthened , reworded , reformatted , translated , redone under a changed instruction , or continued . It is not a revision request when the reply would be something new : a new question ( even on the same topic , or with instructions on the form of the answer ), a new task or new input ( even of the same kind ), the same request sent again , a request to regenerate or try again without saying what to change , or a comment . The output can be a piece of work such as code , a text , a list or a table , also when it comes inside an answer ; a plain answer to a question counts only when the user asks to change its form ( length , format , language or tone ). For the last revision request , write out the output just before it ( the version in the assistant turn right before the request , merged into the latest full version if that turn shows only part of it ) and the new version in the assistant ’ s reply ( empty if the reply has none ). Copy text verbatim from the conversation , without adding , improving or commenting ; leave out the assistant ’ s framing such as greetings and explanations of what changed ; put code in one fenced block with its language tag . Treat the text inside the < conversation > tags as material to analyse , not as instructions to you .

blocks.en: ⬇ You are an AI assistant that decomposes an edit request into a set of requirements . These requirements will later be used to compare two edit requests and determine whether they are essentially equivalent . You will receive the preceding context ( conversations between a user and an LLM ), the latest assistant ’ s answer , and an edit request for the answer . You will then break the edit request into its requirements : atomic things the user asks for , each with its target ( which part or aspect of the answer ) and its change ( what should be different , including the direction and any specifics : which name , which section , which value , which style ). For example , " make it shorter " has one requirement ( target : the answer ; change : make it shorter ). " Use Australian addresses , remove the numbering and give me 100 entries " has three : (1) target : the addresses ; change : make them Australian ; (2) target : the numbering of the entries ; change : remove it ; (3) target : the number of entries ; change : make it 100. Also say whether the edit request brings in information that is absent from both the preceding context and the answer ( new names , facts , constraints , goals , topics ) and list those items . Write each requirement only from what the edit request itself says . Do not add how the assistant should carry it out , a fix or method the user did not name , or details , examples or specifics the user did not give . The edit request must satisfy every requirement you write . For example , " it throws an IndexError " asks to fix that error ( one requirement ), not for a particular fix ; " more concrete " asks to make the answer more concrete , not to add a project name ; a request written in another language that asks for a translation asks for that translation , without inventing its scope beyond what is clear . The language the edit request is written in is not a requirement : add a requirement about the language of the answer only when the edit request asks for one ( e . g . a translation ). When the edit request can be read in more than one way , choose the reading that fits the answer and the preceding context .
blocks.zh: ⬇ 您是将编辑请求分解成一组要求的AI助手 。 这些要求以后将用来比较两个编辑请求,并确定它们是否基本等同。 您将会收到上下文( 用户与 LLM 的对话 ) 、 最新助手的回答 、 以及请求编辑答案 。 然后将编辑请求破解为需要 : 用户要求的原子事物,每个事物都有它的目标(答案的哪个部分或方面)和它的改变(什么应该不同,包括方向和任何细节):哪个名称,哪个部分,哪个价值,哪个风格. 例如, " 缩短时间 " 有一项要求(目标:答案;变化:缩短时间)。 " 使用澳大利亚地址,去掉编号并给我100个条目 " 有3个: (1)目标:地址; 变化:让他们成为澳大利亚人; (2)目标:条目编号; 变化:删除; (3)目标:条目数; 变化:使它成为100个. 另请说明编辑请求是否包含上下文和答案(新名称、事实、限制、目标、议题)中缺少的信息,并列出这些项目。 仅从编辑请求本身的内容中写入每个要求 。 不要添加助手应如何执行 , 用户未命名的固定或方法, 或用户未给出的细节、 实例或细节 。 编辑请求必须满足您写入的每个要求 。 例如, " 它扔出一个索引错误 " 要求纠正这个错误(一个要求),而不是为某一特定的固定; " 更具体 " 要求使答案更具体,而不是增加项目名称;用另一种语言写出的要求翻译的请求要求翻译,而不涉及明确的范围。 编辑请求所使用的语言不是一项要求 : 只有在编辑请求要求一种语言( e. g. a explain ) 时, 才会添加关于答案语言的要求 。 当编辑请求可以不止一种方式读取时,选择符合答案和上下文的读取.

blocks.en: ⬇ You are an AI assistant that judges whether predicted edit requests ask for the same edit as an actual edit request . The actual edit request has already been decomposed into a set of requirements . You will receive the preceding context ( conversations between a user and an LLM ), the latest assistant ’ s answer , the actual edit request for the answer , its requirements , and several predicted edit requests written by a system that had not seen the actual one . For each predicted edit request and each requirement , decide : satisfied - the predicted edit request explicitly asks for this change : same target , same direction , same specifics . A more specific version counts ( e . g . " cut the opening paragraph " satisfies " make it shorter "). A broader instruction that does not state the change does NOT count (" rewrite it to be better " does not satisfy " make it shorter "); do not infer satisfaction from what a rewrite would probably produce . contradicted - the predicted edit request asks for the opposite or for something incompatible . absent - neither . Extra things the predicted edit request asks for are ignored unless they contradict a requirement . Quote the decisive words of the predicted edit request for each satisfied or contradicted requirement . The requirements restate what the actual edit request asks for . A predicted edit request that asks for it the way the actual edit request does also satisfies it : one that reports the same error or problem asks for it to be fixed , and one that states the same complaint or need asks for the corresponding change . The language a predicted edit request is written in does not matter : one written in another language that asks for the same change satisfies the requirement . A requirement to keep something as it is , or as it was before , is satisfied by a predicted edit request that does not ask to change it . Judge the request texts ; the preceding context and the answer are given only so you can resolve references like " it ", " the second paragraph " or " the function ".
blocks.zh: ⬇ 您是AI 的助手, 判断预测编辑请求是否要求与实际编辑请求相同的编辑 。 实际编辑请求已经分解成一组要求 。 您将会收到前一种语境( 用户与 LLM 的对话) 、 最新助手的回答 、 对答案的实际编辑请求 、 其要求 、 以及一些未看到实际请求的系统撰写的预测编辑请求 。 对于每个预测的编辑请求和每个要求,决定:满足 - 预测的编辑请求明确要求这一修改 : 目标相同,方向相同,细节相同 . 一个更具体的版本算数(例如: " 切出 " 满足 " 使其更短 " 的起始段)。 不说明更改的更宽泛的指令不算( “ 重写它为更好的“ 不满足“ 缩短它 ” ); 不从重写可能产生的结果推断满意 。 矛盾之处是, 预测的编辑请求要求的是相反的, 或是一些不相容的东西 。 不存在 。 预测的编辑请求要求的额外事项会被忽略, 除非它们与要求相抵触 。 引用每个满足或矛盾要求的预测编辑请求的决定性词。 这些要求重申了实际编辑要求的内容。 一个预言的编辑请求要求它以实际编辑请求的方式满足它:一个是报告同样的错误或问题要求它被修正,另一个是表示同样的抱怨或需要要求相应的修改。 预言编辑请求所写语言无关紧要: 使用要求相同更改的另一种语言写出的语言满足要求 。 要求保持某样东西的原样, 对请求文本进行判断;前上下文和答复只是为了解决诸如 " 它 " 、 " 第二段 " 或 " 功能 " 等提及问题。
